start_here: Say to your AI: "Sign this Mac app update record with my release key so installed apps accept the update", and give it the record's signed lines joined by newlines. It runs tool:sign-a-mac-app-update and hands you the signature in base64, without the key ever leaving your vault.
no_lists_because: It names no list: it signs the text it is given with the release key held in your vault and answers a name and a signature.
instructions: 1. Keep the Ed25519 release key in your vault under the name mac-app-update-signing-key and grant this tool the program-start capability it asks for.
2. Build the update record's signed lines (version lines, the download address and the file's checksum) and join them with newlines, at most 65536 characters.
3. Say "Sign this update record"; your AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:sign-a-mac-app-update and input {payload}.

4. Read the answer {name: "mac-app-update-signing-key", signature_base64}: a 64 byte Ed25519 signature as 88 base64 characters; put it in the update record as the app reads it. An empty or oversized payload is refused before any call, and a refused vault answers without echoing the run's capability.

worked_examples.title: Signing a five-line update record
worked_examples.ask: Sign this Mac app update record with my release key.
worked_examples.given: From tools/sign-a-mac-app-update/test/sign-a-mac-app-update.test.mjs, which signs this payload with a synthetic Ed25519 key standing in for the vault's key and checks that the signature verifies over the payload bytes. Read from do-work/sign-a-mac-app-update.mjs: the tool sends one held-values:sign call at @held-values for the key mac-app-update-signing-key and converts the engine's 128-digit hex signature to base64. The signature value itself depends on your key, so it is not shown here.
worked_examples.hands_back: {name: "mac-app-update-signing-key", signature_base64: "<88 base64 characters, the 64 byte Ed25519 signature of the payload's UTF-8 bytes>"}, which verifies with the key's public half. A payload of "" answers "Give the text to sign: the record's signed lines, joined by newlines." and nothing reaches the vault.
